summary: The [Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029](2025-05-01 A Blueprint for Mauritius - Digital Transformation 2025-2029) has an inter-ministerial committee behind it and no delivery report, milestone or revision published against it.
developments:
The blueprint was launched in May 2025 with new digital regulations announced alongside it, and an inter-ministerial coordinating committee was established in August 2025 ([blueprint](2025-05-01 A Blueprint for Mauritius - Digital Transformation 2025-2029), [committee](2025-09-01 Mauritius Establishes Inter-Ministerial Committee to Drive Digital Strategy)).

Fifteen months on, nothing has been published against it ([launch](2025-05-26-blueprint-digital-transformation-launch-lexpress), [regulations](2025-09-10 Mauritius Digital Transformation 2025-2029 - A Blueprint and New Digital Regulations)). Its interoperability commitments in particular have produced no instrument, and the framework they would replace dates from 2002.

summary: A [National Data Strategy 2025-2029](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress) was launched in January 2026 and a separate [data governance strategy](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci) was committed to in July, with no text published.
developments:
The data strategy was launched on data protection day around responsible data governance, cybercrime prevention and online protection of minors, with a memorandum signed between the police, the data-protection office and the national computer emergency team ([strategy](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress), [preparation](2025-04-09-ict-data-protection-strategy-in-preparation-lexpress)).

A national data governance strategy was separately committed to at an operator summit in July 2026, alongside forthcoming amendments to the data protection statute aimed at cybersecurity, privacy and online safety for children; no text, timetable or introduction date is published ([commitment](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci)).

summary: A [National AI Strategy and its FAIR guidelines](2026-04-12-national-ai-strategy-fair-guidelines-launch-lexpress) run on six pillars to 2029, with an artificial-intelligence unit from December 2025 and a [first innovation lab](2026-08-21-cajnews-mauritius-ai-innovation-lab-stempower) in August 2026.
developments:
The guidelines are vendor-neutral and border-agnostic, governing by impact rather than geography ([guidelines](2026-04-23-ai-strategy-fair-ethics-before-execution-techcabal), [launch](2026-04-12-national-ai-strategy-fair-guidelines-launch-lexpress)).

The strategy runs 2025-2029 with an artificial-intelligence unit established in December 2025, and a first innovation lab was inaugurated at the cybercity in August 2026 with a memorandum signed at the event; the lab's capacity, funding and access terms are not published ([lab](2026-08-21-cajnews-mauritius-ai-innovation-lab-stempower)).

summary: The [Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021](2021-11-24-mauritius-cybersecurity-cybercrime-act-2021) has been in force since December 2021 and carries the fake-profile, cyberbullying and undesirable-content offences.
developments:
The enacted text as gazetted is held, carrying the offences of misuse of a fake profile, cyberbullying and failure to moderate undesirable content with their penalty scales ([Act](2021-11-24-mauritius-cybersecurity-cybercrime-act-2021)).

It is the statute the ministry's own online-content warnings rest on, and no charge, prosecution or takedown count under any of those sections is published in this base.

progress: Mixed, officer regulations promulgated while the Act itself was left out of an omnibus amending fifty-eight statutes
summary: [Data Protection Officer Regulations](2026-06-12-dpo-regulations-2026-lexpress) were promulgated in June 2026 for January 2027, while the [Data Protection Act 2017](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) is not among the fifty-eight Acts the omnibus amends.
developments:
The regulations formalise designation, qualifications, independence and reporting duties for data protection officers across public and private sectors, with a six-month compliance window ([regulations](2026-06-12-dpo-regulations-2026-lexpress)).

Amendments to the Act itself were committed in July 2026 with no text, timetable or introduction date ([commitment](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci)), and the Act is not among the fifty-eight statutes the omnibus bill amends ([bill](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)). The year's expanded inter-agency data sharing therefore arrives with no matching safeguards amendment ([assessment](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate)).

summary: A [virtual-asset solicitation rule](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) in the omnibus bill would presume any publicly accessible communication targets Mauritius, and [electronic transactions amendments](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac) were referred to in July 2026.
developments:
Unlicensed solicitation of investors would be prohibited by any medium, defined to reach targeted or algorithmic advertising, platforms, applications, social media, influencers, affiliates, referral codes, seminars and webinars, with any publicly accessible communication presumed to target the country; the presumption shifts the burden onto an offshore promoter to show it was not soliciting locally ([rule](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

Amendments modernising the digital-commerce framework and consumer protection were referred to by the minister at a postal-sector workshop, with no text, timetable or introduction date published ([amendments](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac)).

summary: An [omnibus bill](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) of 119 pages amending fifty-eight Acts carries the fintech committee, the artificial-intelligence city scheme, a threat-sharing platform and a digital travel authorisation.
developments:
The bill was introduced on 24 July 2026 with staged commencement from 1 September and several provisions deemed retrospective ([bill](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

A secondary account put the figure at some sixty laws; the enacting text gives fifty-eight amended and one repealed ([account](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees)). It is the single largest legislative vehicle in the country's digital record, and it was introduced and not enacted.

summary: A [Freedom of Information Bill](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress) was announced as in preparation in February 2026, and no draft, text or timetable has been published since.
developments:
The bill was announced by the data-protection commissioner at the launch of the national data strategy ([announcement](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress)).

Six months on, nothing has followed. The country has a data-protection statute aligned to the European regulation and no statutory right of access to public information to sit beside it.

summary: The office runs about [3,000 enforcement actions a year](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate) with 99 per cent resolved amicably, and is [pursuing a European adequacy assessment](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate).
developments:
Enforcement volume was set out at an international identity meeting in May 2026: about 3,000 actions a year, 99 per cent resolved amicably, chief data officers mandated and administrative fines being added by amendment ([enforcement](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate), [formula](2026-05-16 World Bank, African DPAs outline formula for trusted digital identity, DPI)).

Adequacy is being pursued with full alignment of the law to the European regulation, and no application date, assessment stage or decision is published ([adequacy](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate)).

progress: Regressed, large-scale interception still running without judicial oversight while a new plate-recognition system was installed on public premises with no privacy assessment
summary: [Interception described in Parliament as running since 2017 without judicial oversight](2025-02-07-in-the-shadows-of-mass-surveillance-mauritiustimes) has no reform instrument, and an [airport plate-recognition system](2026-08-16-lexpress-mu-aeroport-ssr-systeme-stationnement-anpr) was installed with no retention rule published.
developments:
Large-scale interception was described in Parliament as running since 2017 without judicial oversight, wired into major operators and accessed by counter-terrorism and national security units; no reform instrument, inquiry outcome or judicial-authorisation requirement has been published, and leaked recordings continue to test the framework ([interception](2025-02-07-in-the-shadows-of-mass-surveillance-mauritiustimes), [leaks](2026-07-13-privacy-of-communications-moustass-leaks-mauritiustimes)).

An airport parking system with more than twenty licence-plate-recognition cameras entered full operation in August 2026 at a cost of Rs 50 million, replacing a 2013 installation; no retention period, data controller or privacy assessment is published ([system](2026-08-16-lexpress-mu-aeroport-ssr-systeme-stationnement-anpr)).

progress: Regressed, the state restating criminal exposure for online speech and consulting on identity verification for social media
summary: A [ministerial communique](2026-08-17-lexpress-mu-reseaux-sociaux-sanctions-contenus) restated penalties of up to Rs 1m and twenty years for online content, and [identity verification for social media](2026-06-07-social-media-identity-verification-consultations-lexpress) went to consultation.
developments:
The communique restated that the 2021 Act penalises false profiles, cyber-harassment and the diffusion of undesirable content, that administrators of accounts, pages and groups must moderate flagged content when a competent authority reports it, and that penalties reach a fine of Rs 1m and up to twenty years' penal servitude ([communique](2026-08-17-lexpress-mu-reseaux-sociaux-sanctions-contenus)). It creates no new obligation and is enforcement signalling on a law five years old.

A parallel communique defined undesirable content to include material that is deceptive or inaccurate ([warning](2026-08-17-mitci-mauritius-communique-responsible-use-social-media)).

Consultations opened in June 2026 toward a social-media identity verification mechanism, citing 2,300 online-harm cases in six months and frauds up to Rs 500,000 ([consultation](2026-06-07-social-media-identity-verification-consultations-lexpress)); the minister acknowledged the privacy and free-expression tension and the need to negotiate with platforms ([consultation](2026-06-07-social-media-identity-verification-consultations-lexpress)).

summary: A [national internet governance forum](2026-08-11-mauritius-blockchain-for-good-bybit-igf) convened in 2026 with the Vice President and the minister attending, and the clearest [domestic objection to the AI-first framing](2026-08-02-lexpress-mauritius-needs-faster-justice-not-just-ai) was published in August.
developments:
The forum is a national multi-stakeholder body founded by a civil-society movement; at its 2026 meeting a visiting alliance and an exchange met the Vice President and the minister to discuss artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital-trust frameworks for small island states. The record held is the visiting alliance's own release, and no programme, outcome document or attendance figure is held ([forum](2026-08-11-mauritius-blockchain-for-good-bybit-igf)).

A named analyst argued in August 2026 that contract enforcement rather than technology is what limits the economy, prescribing digitalised case management alongside a small-claims process and a stronger commercial division rather than instead of them ([argument](2026-08-02-lexpress-mauritius-needs-faster-justice-not-just-ai)). It is analysis rather than evidence, and it is the only domestic objection on file to the framing the budget adopts.

progress: Regressed, the continental internet registry seated here left with an unresolved authority chain and an undischarged receiver
summary: The [continental internet registry](2026-08-10-btw-media-afrinic-eight-seat-board-election-evidence-gap) named one person to all eight board seats while withholding the vote tallies its own guidelines promised, and the [appeal court set aside its appeal](2024-10-15-mauritius-afrinic-v-cloud-innovation-2024-scj-473-judgment) for want of corporate authority.
developments:
The appeal court had directed in October 2024 that the board be reconstituted within two months, describing it as a matter of utmost urgency, in substitution for the six months ordered in 2023 ([judgment](2024-10-15-mauritius-afrinic-v-cloud-innovation-2024-scj-473-judgment)).

The registry named a person to all eight seats in September 2025, some nine months past that deadline, while withholding every candidate vote tally its own election guidelines promised ([election](2026-08-10-btw-media-afrinic-eight-seat-board-election-evidence-gap)).

The appeal court then set aside the registry's 2023 appeal for lack of corporate authority without ruling on the official receiver's permission or on statutory leave, leaving the authority chain from election through appointment to quorum unresolved and the receiver undischarged ([appeal](2026-08-13-btw-media-afrinic-appeal-receiver-permission-statutory-leave)).

summary: The [e-Government Interoperability Framework](2002-11-01 Mauritius e-Government Interoperability Framework v1.0) dates from 2002 and no successor is held, twenty-four years on.
developments:
Version 1.0 was published in November 2002 and remains the standing interoperability instrument ([framework](2002-11-01 Mauritius e-Government Interoperability Framework v1.0), [case study](2024-03-01 Enhancing Data-Sharing Practices Between Government Agencies (case study, Sone Osakwe))).

The interoperability commitments of the 2025-2029 blueprint have produced no published instrument. A country running a mobile identity wallet, an instant payment switch and a Tier IV sovereign facility is doing so on an interoperability framework older than any of them.

summary: The postal operator is being wired into a [global postal information-sharing centre](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac) with an international security standard urged, and the state operator co-chairs [model-as-a-service certification work](2026-07-20-mauritius-telecom-tm-forum-modaas-telecomtv).
developments:
The national postal operator is being connected to the postal union's global information-sharing centre and the minister urged adoption of the international information-security management standard; no membership date or commitment is published ([postal](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac)).

Work to define controls and conformance criteria for a model-as-a-service certification framework began in July 2026, with the state operator a founding contributor and co-chair; the framework does not yet exist, and the standards body's own research finds 72 per cent of operator leaders say they trust their production artificial intelligence while 14 per cent can evidence it ([certification](2026-07-20-mauritius-telecom-tm-forum-modaas-telecomtv)).

summary: The [2026-2027 budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) names artificial intelligence thirty-five times and funds a training platform, an investment tax credit and a forensic laboratory; the [Finance Bill](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees) itself is not held.
developments:
The budget carries a 50,000-trainee target, a Rs 25m national learning platform, an investment tax credit of 15 per cent a year over three years, a special economic zone of 83 arpents with preferential data-centre power and thirty-year renewable leases, electronic gates, an electronic visa, an electronic judiciary and a Rs 13m cyber forensic laboratory ([budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

The accompanying 128-page Finance Bill is not held: three fetch paths into the assembly's bills library returned an HTML shell rather than the document, so the enacted tax and revenue measures cannot be read against the announcements ([bill](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees)).

summary: The state operator's [2026-2029 strategy](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress) is a reported Rs 20bn programme across four corridors, and one [payments gateway](2026-05-18 Mauritius emerges as an African payments hub) reports volume growth above 300 per cent.
developments:
The four-corridor strategy covers connectivity, financial services, artificial intelligence and compute, and innovation, at a reported Rs 20bn; no delivery milestone has been published against it ([strategy](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress), [launch](2025-12-08-mauritius-telecom-connect-strategy-launch-techafricanews)).

One cross-border payments gateway reports its Mauritian entity grew transaction volume by over 300 per cent year on year and merchants by 42 per cent, serving over 150 companies, crediting exit from an international financial watchlist for the confidence ([gateway](2026-05-18 Mauritius emerges as an African payments hub)); the figures are the company's own ([gateway](2026-05-18 Mauritius emerges as an African payments hub)).

summary: A [development agency annual report](2026-08-25-undp-mauritius-annual-report-2025) for 2025 is held in full, and its digital component is not separately costed.
developments:
The report is a United Nations development agency's own account of its year in the country ([report](2026-08-25-undp-mauritius-annual-report-2025)).

The digital component is not separately costed in what is held, so the base can record that a partner is present and not what it spends on digital work. It is the only development-partner financing record in this unit.

summary: [Two ageing cables carry most international traffic](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur); a [new cable participation](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur) rests on a non-disclosure agreement, and [two further landings](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress) are named in an operator strategy.
developments:
Landings exist on four systems, two of which carry most international traffic, and the stated driver for new capacity is infrastructure ageing, with one cable due to retire around 2027 ([cables](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur), [estate](2025-07-16-hyperscale-data-hub-data-centres-telecomreviewafrica)).

The prime-ministerial commitment to join a new transoceanic cable sits behind a signed non-disclosure agreement and unfinished technical, legal and financial negotiation; no consortium confirmation, landing point, capacity, cost or service date is published, and the operator's own chief executive stayed non-specific on subsea at the same event ([commitment](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur), [summit](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci), [report](2026-07-16-mauritius-joins-america-india-connect-cable)).

Two further landings are named as planned in the operator's strategy, one of them to replace the retiring cable, with no contract, cost or date published ([landings](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress)).

summary: The [satellite authorisation regime](2025-05-22-mauritius-icta-ngso-satellite-decision) requires a locally licensed provider, a local point of presence and provider-retained terminals, and no service has been authorised under it.
developments:
The regulator's decision of May 2025 permits service only through a locally licensed provider, with a local point of presence carrying Mauritian-geolocated addresses, real-time terminal dashboards and provider-retained terminal ownership ([decision](2025-05-22-mauritius-icta-ngso-satellite-decision)).

No satellite service has been authorised under it. Domestic experts are divided on its relevance given the country's existing fibre and mobile coverage ([debate](2026-07-02-mauritius-starlink-debate-defi-media)), which is the argument a small dense island makes against low-orbit service that larger neighbours cannot.

The ICT authority awarded a two-year contract on 28 August 2026 to provide satellite-based internet and communications to Raphael Island in the St Brandon archipelago, a first for the archipelago, intended to strengthen maritime monitoring, meteorological capability and safety in a cyclone-prone area ([contract](2026-08-28-platformafrica-emtel-icta-st-brandon-connectivity)). No service date, capacity or contract value is stated.

summary: [Ten facilities operate across five locations](2025-07-16-hyperscale-data-hub-data-centres-telecomreviewafrica), unchanged in count for a year, and a [carrier-neutral green data centre](2026-08-19-lexpress-mu-sadc-ramgoolam-carrier-neutral-green-centre) was announced at a regional summit in August 2026.
developments:
The estate is ten operating data centres across five towns, including a carrier-neutral facility designed to the highest resilience tier and the internet exchange point; no new facility has been reported since ([estate](2025-07-16-hyperscale-data-hub-data-centres-telecomreviewafrica)).

A carrier-neutral green data centre and a digital embassy village were announced at a regional summit in August 2026 as the digital leg of a bid to position the country as a regional hub, with no site, capacity, cost, operator or date stated ([announcement](2026-08-19-lexpress-mu-sadc-ramgoolam-carrier-neutral-green-centre)).

summary: The [Rose-Belle facility](2025-12-31-rose-belle-tier-iv-data-centre-national-strategy-lexpress) was certified to the highest resilience tier in December 2025 and hosts the government portal, the identity wallet and government artificial-intelligence workloads.
developments:
It hosts electronic health, the government portal, the mobile identity wallet, the penalty-points licence system and government artificial-intelligence workloads, giving the ageing government online centre the disaster recovery it lacked ([facility](2025-12-31-rose-belle-tier-iv-data-centre-national-strategy-lexpress)).

It is the country's sovereign-hosting anchor and the base holds no capacity, utilisation or tenant figure for it.

summary: The [2026-2027 budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) provides a special economic zone of 83 arpents with preferential data-centre power and thirty-year renewable leases.
developments:
The zone is the country's only stated arrangement connecting energy supply to data-centre siting ([budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

No generation commitment, tariff, water assessment or outage measure for any facility is published, so the incentive is on record and the supply behind it is not.

summary: A [critical information infrastructure regime](2026-05-22-cybersecurity-critical-infrastructure-regulations-2026-lexpress) came into force in June 2026 across six sectors, a [threat-sharing platform](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) is provided for, and a [forensic laboratory](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) is funded.
developments:
The designation regulations are in force across financial and banking, public service, information technology and broadcasting, energy and water, and transport, with a twelve-month compliance window and non-compliance carrying up to twenty-five years' imprisonment and fines up to Rs 2m ([regime](2026-05-22-cybersecurity-critical-infrastructure-regulations-2026-lexpress), [framework](2026-06-30-cii-cyber-laws-framework-itweb)).

The omnibus bill would empower the central bank to establish a cyber threat intelligence sharing platform and to require financial institutions, and other institutions it specifies, to participate on terms it determines; participation is compulsory and the perimeter is set by the central bank rather than by the cyber authority ([platform](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

A cyber forensic laboratory is funded at Rs 13m alongside an information-security management system across the administration, with no site, staffing or opening date published ([laboratory](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)), against more than 4,000 reported cyber incidents since January 2026 ([incidents](2026-08-14-mauritius-telecom-cybersecurity-ai-schools-programme)).

summary: The Finance Bill would empower the [statistics office to share more data with the finance ministry](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees), alongside new declaration duties on public bodies.
developments:
The provision was before Parliament in July 2026 and its enacting text is not held ([provision](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees)).

The expanded inter-agency sharing arrives with no matching amendment to the data protection statute, and the interoperability framework it would run over dates from 2002. Those two facts together are the exchange position of this unit.

summary: The [Mobile ID wallet](2024-09-06 Mauritius Launches Mobile ID Digital Wallet with Thales - First African ISO-standard Digital ID Wallet) has been in service since September 2024 and is hosted on the sovereign facility, with no user or issuance figure published.
developments:
The wallet launched in September 2024 with a foreign vendor under the 2024 national identity card regulations ([launch](2024-09-06 Mauritius Launches Mobile ID Digital Wallet with Thales - First African ISO-standard Digital ID Wallet), [regulations](2024-01-01 National Identity Card (Mobile ID) Regulations 2024 (Mauritius))).

It is now hosted on the Rose-Belle facility and still carries no published user or issuance figure. A domestic analysis welcomed its convenience and pressed for privacy and surveillance safeguards around the enabling regulations ([analysis](2025-02-06 Smart and Mobile ID in Mauritius - Recommendations for a Balanced Approach)).

summary: [SIM registration by electronic identity check](2024-01-01 eKYC Steps for Mauritian Citizen (SIM Re-Registration)) has been in use since the re-registration exercise, with no completion or coverage figure held.
developments:
The electronic verification steps were published for the re-registration exercise and remain in use ([steps](2024-01-01 eKYC Steps for Mauritian Citizen (SIM Re-Registration))).

No completion or coverage figure is held, and no other system is recorded taking the national identity as its authentication, so the identity layer's reach into other sectors cannot be established from this base.

summary: The omnibus bill would make [permits issuable in digital, card or paper form](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) and impose a digital travel authorisation on visa-exempt arrivals.
developments:
The authorisation would be applied for electronically and paid before travel; the bill was introduced and not enacted ([provision](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

It is the first credential in the base whose form is set by statute rather than by the issuing agency, which is what makes the digital form enforceable rather than optional.

summary: The [civil registration base](2024-01-01 Mauritius Civil Status Division Annual Report on Performance FY2023-2024) is recorded as complete and underpinning the identity system, on a performance report for 2023-2024.
developments:
The civil status division's performance report for 2023-2024 is the most recent account held ([report](2024-01-01 Mauritius Civil Status Division Annual Report on Performance FY2023-2024), [presentation](2019-06-01 The CRVS and Identity Eco-System in the Republic of Mauritius (presentation))).

No later performance report is held, and no registration rate, backlog or error measure has been published since. A complete base is the assumption on which the identity wallet and the social-security digitisation both rest.

summary: A [National Fintech Strategy 2026-2030](2026-06-29-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030-wearetech) was presented in June 2026, a [governance committee](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) put on a statutory footing, and a [digital onboarding system](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress) is under construction.
developments:
The strategy runs six pillars carrying a governance committee, open banking, an artificial-intelligence push in finance and a business facilitation bill, implemented with the central bank ([strategy](2026-06-29-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030-wearetech)).

The committee is provided for in a new part of the financial services statute from September 2026, minister-chaired, seating the central bank governor, the financial regulator's chief executive, two ministries, the investment board and four private-sector members, empowered to approve sector-wide standards and expressly not a body corporate ([committee](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026), [account](2026-06-29-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030-wearetech)).

A know-your-customer system for digital onboarding is under construction alongside alignment to an international cross-border roadmap and exploratory work on fraud detection, with no delivery date published ([onboarding](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress)).

summary: The [instant payment switch](2024-01-01 SIIPS 2024 Case Study - MauCAS (Mauritius)) is a mature interoperable rail with a code standard, and the largest bank reports [code payments up 67 per cent](2026-01-19-mcb-qr-payments-67pc-growth-lexpress) with cash down to 27 per cent of consumer spend.
developments:
The switch was profiled as a mature interoperable national rail with a code standard in a 2024 instant-payments review, and no national transaction volume has been published since ([switch](2024-01-01 SIIPS 2024 Case Study - MauCAS (Mauritius))).

The largest bank's 2025 figures put cash at 27 per cent of consumer spend against 30 per cent a year earlier, code payments up 67 per cent year on year, contactless above six in ten card transactions and about 18,000 merchants accepting ([adoption](2026-01-19-mcb-qr-payments-67pc-growth-lexpress)); they are one bank's figures rather than a national series ([adoption](2026-01-19-mcb-qr-payments-67pc-growth-lexpress)).

progress: No change, a first published user count with nothing earlier behind it
summary: The state operator's wallet reports [over 130,000 active users](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress), being built into a cross-border product, with no transaction figure published.
developments:
The figure comes from the operator's 2026-2029 strategy ([wallet](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress)).

No earlier user count is held, so the level is recorded and the direction is not. It is the only wallet uptake figure in the base for a country whose broadband penetration is above saturation, which makes the wallet the laggard rather than the network.

summary: An [India payment link](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress) has run since 2024, a [Seychelles corridor](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica) was announced in July 2026, and the rupee is [reported as considered](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking) for regional settlement.
developments:
The bilateral cross-border payments link with India was the country's first, in force since February 2024, with no volume or corridor figure published ([link](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress)).

A corridor with Seychelles was announced as launched by the state operator at its summit, with no corroborating record from the partner, the central bank or the counterpart central bank on file ([corridor](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica)).

Onboarding the rupee to the regional settlement system is reported as under consideration, potentially by the end of 2027, on a spokesperson's account from another central bank; no domestic statement is held, and the named next currencies are two others ([settlement](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking)).

summary: [10.5m social-benefit documents](2026-06-02-e-social-security-digitization-welfare-wearetech) are being digitised into a future platform, after thirteen years of the welfare system running on paper.
developments:
Bulk scanning of beneficiary files began in May 2026 with full integration stated at about eighteen months; the system carries about 800,000 payments a month to at least 350,000 beneficiaries ([digitisation](2026-06-02-e-social-security-digitization-welfare-wearetech)).

Social-protection spending was Rs 91.4bn, 12.8 per cent of gross domestic product, in 2024-25 ([spending](2026-06-02-e-social-security-digitization-welfare-wearetech)), which is the scale the paper system was carrying.

summary: The [eHealth strategy](2015-01-01 Health 2015 - Seamless Continuity of Care (Mauritius eHealth strategy)) dates from 2015 and no successor or delivery report is held, though health workloads now run on the sovereign facility.
developments:
The continuity-of-care strategy published in 2015 is the standing instrument ([strategy](2015-01-01 Health 2015 - Seamless Continuity of Care (Mauritius eHealth strategy))).

Electronic health workloads are hosted on the Rose-Belle facility, so the hosting has moved and the strategy governing what is hosted has not. No successor strategy, delivery report, record count or facility coverage figure is held.

summary: The [education pilot](2026-01-26-mytgpt-education-pilot-techreviewafrica) on the sovereign artificial-intelligence platform was narrowed from a student tutor to a teacher assistant after teacher and parent resistance.
developments:
The pilot was deliberately narrowed on pedagogical rather than technical grounds to homework correction and exam generation, targeting one per secondary teacher by 2027 ([pilot](2026-01-26-mytgpt-education-pilot-techreviewafrica), [keynote](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica)).

The operator's chief executive put the platform's exam-marking tools at 99 per cent accuracy across the tools introduced ([interview](2026-08-16-mauritius-telecom-ceo-aws-partnership-interview)). It is a rare documented narrowing of an African education deployment, and the reason it narrowed is recorded ([argument](2026-07-13-gungadin-ai-economic-pillar-interview-mauritiustimes)).

summary: An [online motor vehicle licence and road tax service](2026-08-18-mauritius-online-licensing-road-tax-taxis) launched in August 2026, with [electronic gates, visa and judiciary](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) funded and a [clinical-trial licensing system](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) provided for in statute.
developments:
The licence and road tax service is live for taxi operators, who renew and pay online instead of at post offices and counters, and the ministry states it will also build a database of operators; the transport authority's underlying system is stated as outdated with a tender launched to upgrade it ([service](2026-08-18-mauritius-online-licensing-road-tax-taxis)).

Electronic gates, an electronic visa and an electronic judiciary are funded in the budget alongside a healthcare innovation and artificial-intelligence unit, with no procurement, vendor or delivery date published ([funding](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

The omnibus bill would put concurrent submission, review and processing of clinical-trial applications through a statutory electronic system, with the council and ethics committee empowered to meet virtually; the electronic channel and the procedure that runs on it are in the same statute, which makes the channel enforceable against the regulator ([licensing](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)). A metrology platform for bookings, payments and certificates is separately in build ([metrology](2026-08-10-mauritius-legal-metrology-digitization)).

summary: A [sovereign artificial-intelligence platform](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica) is in service, an [AI registry](2026-07-12-mauritius-telecom-airegistry-mu-launch-journaldudimanche) went live in July 2026, and a [Mauritian Creole voice model](2026-08-16-mauritius-telecom-ceo-aws-partnership-interview) was presented in August.
developments:
The registry is live as a discovery and trust directory of locally relevant models, agents and skills that does not host or sell what it lists, each entry carrying provider identity, local-context relevance and any institutional validation; the stack is open-sourced and is being offered to other operators ([registry](2026-07-12-mauritius-telecom-airegistry-mu-launch-journaldudimanche)).

The operator's chief executive set out a cloud partnership with a hyperscaler, sovereign data centres and a plan to train 50,000 people ([platform](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica)).

A voice model for Mauritian Creole was described by the incumbent operator as the first built for the language; the account is the chief executive's in an interview and no user count, evaluation or release detail is held ([model](2026-08-16-mauritius-telecom-ceo-aws-partnership-interview)).

summary: The [FAIR guidelines](2026-04-23-ai-strategy-fair-ethics-before-execution-techcabal) carry mandatory bias audits in financial services and gaming and locally-based-representative duties on foreign providers, non-binding but on a stated legal trajectory.
developments:
The guidelines govern by impact rather than geography, which is what lets them reach a foreign provider serving the country ([guidelines](2026-04-23-ai-strategy-fair-ethics-before-execution-techcabal)).

They are non-binding on a stated legal trajectory, so what the base records is an obligation the state intends to make enforceable and has not yet. No audit, complaint or enforcement action under them is published ([launch](2026-04-12-national-ai-strategy-fair-guidelines-launch-lexpress)).

summary: An [AI City Scheme](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) in the omnibus bill would certify a specialised hub carrying fiscal incentives, expedited permits and a founder permit at US$1m invested.
developments:
The certificate would cover a specialised technological and innovation hub promoting artificial intelligence, digital sectors, advanced computing infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, carrying fiscal incentives, duty exemptions, expedited permits and prescribed property acquisition, with a new founder occupation permit at US$1m invested ([scheme](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

It is an incentive and immigration scheme rather than a governance one, and it was introduced and not enacted. No existing hub, incubator or accelerator is separately recorded for the country.

progress: Mixed, the sector at about half its stated ambition while no picture of enterprise adoption exists at all
summary: The sector is put at [about 5.4 per cent of gross domestic product](2026-07-29-mauritius-launches-ai-readiness-survey) against a stated ambition of 10 to 12, and an [adoption and readiness survey](2026-07-29-mauritius-launches-ai-readiness-survey) was commissioned because no picture exists.
developments:
The share was stated by the minister in July 2026 against an ambition of 10 to 12 per cent ([share](2026-07-29-mauritius-launches-ai-readiness-survey)).

An adoption, readiness and governance study was launched on 27 July 2026 by the chamber of commerce, the outsourcing association and a third partner, commissioned because no picture exists of adoption levels, affected sectors or available skills; its results are not held ([study](2026-07-28-mauritius-mcci-otam-ai-adoption-readiness-governance-survey), [launch](2026-07-29-mauritius-launches-ai-readiness-survey)).

A country doubling its sector share is a policy ambition; a country that cannot say what its firms have adopted is a measurement problem, and both are on the record here.

summary: A [national training target of 50,000 people in one year](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) covers professionals, ninth-grade pupils, teachers and civil servants on a Rs 25m platform.
developments:
The target breaks down as 25,000 professionals, 12,000 ninth-grade pupils, 8,000 teachers and 5,000 civil servants ([target](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

No completion or enrolment figure has been published. It is the largest single skills commitment in the base for the country and the base holds no baseline of current skills against which to read it.

summary: A [schools cybersecurity and artificial-intelligence awareness programme](2026-08-14-mauritius-telecom-cybersecurity-ai-schools-programme) opened in August 2026 with about 500 senior secondary students across all four education zones.
developments:
The programme is run by the incumbent operator with the education ministry and opened on 13 August 2026, with free ten-hour cloud-provider training on offer ([programme](2026-08-14-mauritius-telecom-cybersecurity-ai-schools-programme), [account](2026-08-14-mauritius-cybersecurity-ai-students-lexpress)).

It is an operator-run awareness programme rather than a curriculum change, and no full-year target, budget or evaluation is stated.

summary: [Rodrigues was brought into the national digital strategy](2026-05-29-rodrigues-port-mathurin-ai-cybersecurity-mission-lexpress) in May 2026 through a cybersecurity framework, a youth project and post-office access to the national sign-on.
developments:
A ministerial mission to the island in May 2026 agreed a cybersecurity working framework with a mainland-based team and a dedicated representative, a youth awareness project, and integration of the national sign-on and super-app through post office agents, building on the regional assembly's own roadmap ([mission](2026-05-29-rodrigues-port-mathurin-ai-cybersecurity-mission-lexpress)).

It is the first national digital commitment to the outer island on record. No connectivity, usage or service-uptake figure for it is published.

summary: A [national fisheries information system](2026-08-21-lexpress-mu-systeme-information-integre-peches-cotieres) was endorsed at a validation workshop in August 2026 for submission to a multilateral funding window.
developments:
The proposal was endorsed at a workshop convened by the fisheries ministry, for submission under a fisheries fund's project-implementation grant window ([proposal](2026-08-21-lexpress-mu-systeme-information-integre-peches-cotieres)).

It is a proposal for submission with no award, budget or build on record. It is the only sectoral data system in this unit that would produce statistics rather than administer a service.

summary: A [hyperscaler memorandum](2026-07-16-allmyt-summit-2026-techreviewafrica) was signed with soft scope and no disclosed value, and another hyperscaler [already operates a ground station](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur) on the island.
developments:
The memorandum was executed at a summit opening ceremony in July 2026 covering skills, institutional enablement and a growth pathway for local innovators, with no disclosed value or binding deliverable; the training is to run initially in premises rented for the purpose, with permanent infrastructure only a possibility ([memorandum](2026-07-16-allmyt-summit-2026-techreviewafrica), [summit](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur)).

The other hyperscaler already operates a ground station serviced by the state operator, so a cable commitment would deepen a relationship rather than open one; what is contracted with either so far is skills and confidentiality, not capacity ([presence](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur)).

summary: A [preferential buyers credit of US$73.7m](2018-01-01-eximbank-cn-mus-001-china-eximbank-provides-737-million-preferential) is the largest external digital-sector financing on the country's record, with no repayment or completion statement published.
developments:
The credit is recorded in the finance ministry's own annual report ([credit](2018-01-01-eximbank-cn-mus-001-china-eximbank-provides-737-million-preferential)).

Eight years on, no repayment, drawdown or completion statement has been published, and no other Chinese instrument, vendor contract or cooperation framework is recorded for the country.

summary: The European relationship on file is a [data-protection adequacy assessment](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate) being pursued in 2026, with no application date, stage or decision published.
developments:
Adequacy is being pursued with full alignment of the law to the European regulation, confirmed by the data-protection commissioner in May 2026 ([assessment](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate)).

No application date, assessment stage or decision is published, and no European funding instrument, memorandum or project for the country's digital programme is held. The relationship is regulatory rather than financial, which is unusual in this base.

summary: The [first bilateral cross-border payments agreement](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress) was with India in February 2024, and a [new transoceanic cable](2026-07-16-mauritius-joins-america-india-connect-cable) would run between the two countries.
developments:
The payments link has been in force since February 2024 as the country's first such agreement, with no volume or corridor figure published since ([link](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress)).

The cable participation commitment is to a system connecting the United States and India, behind which sits a signed non-disclosure agreement and unfinished negotiation ([cable](2026-07-16-mauritius-joins-america-india-connect-cable)). Between them these are the country's two named Indian engagements, one operating and unmeasured, one committed and unsigned.

summary: Cabinet approved a [Saudi energy and cybersecurity memorandum](2026-08-02-energie-un-partenariat-strategique-en-preparation-avec-larabie-saoudite) for signature in August 2026, putting digital transformation and energy-sector cybersecurity alongside hydrocarbons.
developments:
It is an approval to sign rather than a signature, with no signing date, term, value or committed system, standard or spend ([memorandum](2026-08-02-energie-un-partenariat-strategique-en-preparation-avec-larabie-saoudite)).

It is the only Gulf engagement on record for the country, and the digital element is bundled inside an energy instrument rather than standing on its own.
